title: Media: broadcast
question: Which verb means to send out a programme on television or radio so that people can watch or listen?
explanation: To 'broadcast' is to send out a programme on TV or radio. 'Publish' and 'print' are used for written material, and 'advertise' means to promote a product.

title: Media: headline
question: 'The story made ___ in every newspaper.' Which word fits?
explanation: The fixed expression is 'to make headlines'. A story has a title, a caption goes with a photo, and a slogan is a catchphrase in advertising.

title: Media: the press
question: Which phrase refers to journalists and news organisations collectively?
explanation: 'The press' is the collective term for journalists and news organisations. 'The public' means ordinary people, 'the authorities' means officials, and 'the audience' means people watching or listening.

title: Media: coverage
question: 'There was extensive media ___ of the election.' Which word fits?
explanation: 'Media coverage' is the standard collocation for the amount of reporting an event receives. The other nouns do not combine with 'media' in this meaning.

title: Media: journalist
question: Which word means a person whose job is to gather information and write news stories?
explanation: A 'journalist' gathers information and writes news stories. A 'novelist' writes fiction, a 'publisher' produces and sells books or papers, and a 'librarian' works in a library.

title: Media: article
question: 'She wrote an ___ about climate change for the magazine.' Which word fits?
explanation: An 'article' is a piece of writing in a magazine or newspaper. An 'edition' is one issue of a publication, an 'episode' is one part of a TV series, and an 'index' is a list at the back of a book.

title: Media: streaming
question: Which word means watching video or listening to audio online as it arrives, without saving it to your device?
explanation: 'Streaming' means playing media online as it arrives. 'Downloading' saves a copy on your device, 'uploading' sends a file to the internet, and 'scrolling' means moving up and down a page.

title: Media: social media
question: Which term means websites and apps where users share posts and photos with friends?
explanation: 'Social media' means platforms where users create and share content. 'Mass media' is a general term for news channels reaching large audiences, 'print media' means newspapers and magazines, and 'broadcast media' means TV and radio.

title: Media: subscribe
question: 'You need to ___ to the channel to get notifications.' Which word fits?
explanation: You 'subscribe to' a channel to follow it. 'Enrol' is used for courses and takes 'on' or 'in', 'attend' takes a direct object, and 'admit' means to confess or allow in.

title: Media: viewer
question: Which word means a person who watches television?
explanation: A 'viewer' watches television. A 'listener' hears radio, a 'reader' reads, and a 'visitor' goes to a place.

title: Culture: exhibition
question: Which word means a public display of art or objects in a gallery or museum?
explanation: An 'exhibition' is a public display of art or objects. An 'auction' is a sale to the highest bidder, an 'audition' is a test performance and a 'workshop' is a practical training session.

title: Culture: performance
question: Which word means an occasion when actors, musicians, or dancers perform live for an audience?
explanation: A 'performance' is a live show for an audience. A 'rehearsal' is practice, an 'audition' is a test to get a role, and a 'review' is a written opinion.

title: Culture: audience
question: Which word means the group of people watching a show, film, or concert?
explanation: The 'audience' is the group watching a show. The 'cast' is the actors, 'critics' write opinions about it, and 'staff' are the people who work at the venue.

title: Culture: review
question: Which word means a written critical evaluation of a film, book, or show?
explanation: A 'review' gives a critical opinion. A 'trailer' is a short promotional clip, a 'synopsis' is a plain summary of the plot, and a 'script' is the written text of a film or play.

title: Culture: bestseller
question: Which word means a book that sells a very large number of copies?
explanation: A 'bestseller' is a book that sells very many copies. A 'classic' is a book valued over a long time, a 'paperback' is a type of binding, and a 'manuscript' is an author's unpublished text.

title: Culture: sculpture
question: 'There was a large bronze ___ in the centre of the park.' Which word fits?
explanation: A 'sculpture' is a three-dimensional artwork, often made of bronze. A 'painting', 'poster' and 'mural' are flat images and are not made of bronze.

title: Culture: genre
question: 'Horror, comedy, and romance are all examples of different ___.' Which word fits?
explanation: 'Genres' are categories of films or books, such as horror, comedy and romance. 'Scenes', 'plots' and 'roles' are parts of a single story, not categories.

title: Culture: rehearsal
question: Which word means a practice session held before a performance?
explanation: A 'rehearsal' is a practice session before a performance. An 'audition' is a test for a role, a 'premiere' is the first public performance, and an 'interval' is a break during a show.

title: Technology: app
question: Which word means a program that you install and use on a smartphone?
explanation: An 'app' is short for 'application', a program on a phone. An 'icon' is the small picture you tap to open it, a 'file' stores data, and a 'folder' holds files.

title: Technology: download
question: Which word means to copy a file from the internet onto your own device?
explanation: To 'download' is to transfer a file from a remote server to your device. 'Upload' is the opposite direction, 'install' means to set up software after copying it, and 'refresh' means to reload a page.

title: Technology: update
question: Which word means to install the latest version of software you already have?
explanation: To 'update' software is to install its latest version. To 'uninstall' is to remove it, 'delete' is to erase it and 'reboot' is to restart the device.

title: Technology: device
question: Which word is the general term for a piece of electronic equipment such as a phone or tablet?
explanation: A 'device' is a piece of electronic equipment. A 'platform' is a system software runs on, a 'network' links computers and a 'program' is software.

title: Technology: password
question: Which word means a secret string of characters used to access an account?
explanation: A 'password' is a secret string of characters used to access an account. A 'username' is not secret, a 'profile' is a page of personal details and a 'signature' is text added to emails.

title: Technology: software
question: Which word means the programs and apps that run on a computer, as opposed to its physical parts?
explanation: 'Software' means programs and apps. 'Hardware' means the physical parts, a 'network' connects computers and 'bandwidth' is the amount of data a connection can carry.

title: Technology: data
question: Which word means information collected and stored in digital form?
explanation: 'Data' is information stored in digital form. 'Code' is the instructions programmers write, a 'signal' carries information through a medium, and an 'icon' is a small picture.

title: Technology: charge
question: 'I need to ___ my phone before we leave — the battery is almost empty.' Which word fits?
explanation: You 'charge' a phone to restore its battery. 'Fill' and 'refuel' are used for tanks, and 'load' is used for putting data or goods onto something.

title: Technology: screen
question: Which word means the flat glass surface of a phone or tablet that displays images?
explanation: The 'screen' is the glass surface that displays images. The 'keyboard' is for typing, the 'speaker' produces sound and the 'battery' provides power.

title: Technology: Wi-Fi
question: 'Is there free ___ in the hotel so I can check my email?' Which word fits?
explanation: 'Wi-Fi' gives wireless internet access. 'Bluetooth' connects devices over short distances, 'GPS' shows location and 'USB' is a cable connection, so none of them lets you check email through the hotel's internet.

title: Internet: website
question: Which word means a collection of connected web pages at a single address?
explanation: A 'website' is a collection of connected web pages at one address. A 'browser' is the program you use to view it, a 'server' is the computer that stores it and a 'cookie' is a small file a site saves on your device.

title: Internet: online
question: 'More and more people prefer to shop ___ instead of in physical stores.' Which word fits?
explanation: 'Shop online' means to buy over the internet. 'Offline' means not connected, 'inline' means in a row, and 'onboard' means on a ship or plane or joining a team.

title: Internet: link
question: Which word means a clickable URL that takes you to another web page?
explanation: A 'link' is a clickable item that takes you to another page. A 'tab' is a page open in a browser, a 'cursor' is the pointer on the screen and an 'icon' is a small picture.

title: Internet: search engine
question: Which phrase means a service like Google that helps you find information online?
explanation: A 'search engine' finds information on the web. A 'web browser' displays pages, a 'social network' connects people and an 'app store' sells apps.

title: Internet: blog
question: Which word means a regularly updated website with informal articles by one author or a small group?
explanation: A 'blog' is a website with regular informal posts by one author or a small group. A 'podcast' is audio, a 'forum' is a discussion board with many contributors and a 'wiki' is a collaborative reference site.

title: Internet: post
question: 'She wrote a ___ on social media about her holiday and tagged her friends.' Which word fits?
explanation: A 'post' is something you publish on social media. A 'poster' is a large printed notice, a 'postcard' is a card sent by mail and a 'postman' delivers letters.

title: Internet: notification
question: Which word means an alert from an app telling you about new activity, such as a new message?
explanation: A 'notification' is an alert from an app. A 'subscription' is a paid or followed service, an 'invitation' is a request to attend and a 'password' is a secret code.

title: Communication: text message
question: Which phrase means a short written message sent from one phone to another?
explanation: A 'text message' is a short written message sent between phones. A 'phone call', 'voicemail' and 'video call' use spoken words, not written ones.

title: Communication: attachment
question: A file sent together with an email is called an email ___.
explanation: An 'attachment' is a file sent with an email. A 'signature' is text added at the end, the 'subject' is the title line and the 'inbox' is where received emails arrive.

title: Communication: reply
question: 'I clicked ___ to respond to her email.' Which word fits?
explanation: 'Reply' sends a response to the sender. 'Forward' sends the email on to someone else, 'delete' removes it and 'archive' stores it away.

title: Communication: forward
question: 'I received the invitation — let me ___ it to you.' Which word fits?
explanation: 'Forward' means to send a received email on to someone else. 'Reply' answers the sender, 'delete' removes the email and 'save' keeps it.

title: Communication: voicemail
question: Which word means a recorded spoken message left when someone doesn't answer their phone?
explanation: 'Voicemail' is a recorded message left when no one answers. A 'ringtone' is the sound a phone makes, a 'hotline' is a direct phone service and a 'headset' is headphones with a microphone.

title: Arts: gallery
question: Which word means a place that displays and sells works of art?
explanation: A 'gallery' displays and sells works of art. A 'studio' is where an artist works, an 'auditorium' is a hall for audiences and a 'library' lends books.

title: Arts: portrait
question: 'The artist painted a ___ of the queen showing only her face and shoulders.' Which word fits?
explanation: A 'portrait' shows a person, here the queen's face and shoulders. A 'landscape' shows scenery, a 'still life' shows objects and a 'sketchbook' is a book for drawing.

title: Arts: lyrics
question: Which word means the words of a song?
explanation: 'Lyrics' are the words of a song. The 'melody' is the tune, the 'rhythm' is the pattern of beats and 'harmony' is notes sounding together.

title: Music: orchestra
question: Which word means a large group of musicians playing classical instruments together?
explanation: An 'orchestra' is a large group of musicians playing instruments. A 'choir' is a group of singers, a 'quartet' is four performers and a 'duet' is two.

title: Music: concert
question: Which word means a live musical performance given for an audience?
explanation: A 'concert' is a live musical performance. A 'lecture' is a talk, an 'audition' is a test performance and an 'exhibition' is a display of art or objects.

title: Music: instrument
question: 'She plays three musical ___ — the piano, the violin and the guitar.' Which word fits?
explanation: 'Instruments' are things you play to make music, such as the piano, violin and guitar. 'Pieces' are compositions, 'genres' are styles and 'notes' are single sounds.

title: Media: commercial
question: Which word means a short paid advertisement shown between television programmes?
explanation: A 'commercial' is a paid TV advertisement. A 'documentary' is a factual programme, an 'episode' is one part of a series and a 'bulletin' is a short news report.

title: Technology: tablet
question: Which word means a portable flat touchscreen device with no physical keyboard, used for reading and browsing?
explanation: A 'tablet' is a flat touchscreen device with no physical keyboard. A 'laptop' and a 'desktop' have keyboards, and a 'console' is a gaming machine.

title: Internet: account
question: 'You need to create an ___ before you can use the streaming service.' Which word fits?
explanation: You 'create an account' to register for a service. An 'adapter' connects equipment, an 'alarm' gives a warning signal and an 'address' says where something is.

title: Culture: festival
question: Which word means a large public event celebrating music, arts or culture, often lasting several days?
explanation: A 'festival' is a large public event celebrating music, arts or culture. A 'tournament' is a sports competition, a 'marathon' is a long race and an 'auction' is a sale.
